prompt: Develop a Shoreline Property Operations Console system for offline, enterprise property teams to manage resident move-outs, deposits, document evidence, and on-site logistics with auditable workflows. Primary roles include Administrator (configures rules, permissions, and templates), Property Manager (runs daily operations and approves settlements), Leasing/Front Desk Staff (check-in/out parcels and collect resident submissions), Reviewer/Auditor (read-only access with export), and Resident Liaison (enters resident-provided profile/preferences during interactions). The desktop app runs on Windows 11 with an English UI, supports 1920x1080+ with high-DPI scaling, and installs via a signed .msi. Desktop-first interaction is required: multi-window workspaces for “Move-Out Case,” “Parcel Queue,” and “Claims Inbox” running in parallel; right-click context menus for status transitions and attachment actions; global keyboard shortcuts (e.g., Ctrl+K quick search, Ctrl+Shift+N new case, F2 rename tag); and a system-tray mode for background timers and reminders without network push. The solution must include a claim and matching workflow engine to resolve disputes (e.g., parcel ownership or deposit deductions) using rule-based similarity across category, unit address, time window, and keywords; users can submit/withdraw claims, attach proofs, and complete two-party confirmation with closed-loop statuses. Timeouts are enforced: if the counterparty does not respond within 72 hours, the claim auto-cancels and can be reopened once with manager approval. End-to-end parcel lifecycle management must provide a configurable state machine for check-in, check-out, delivery, receipt confirmation, return/exception, capturing operator, timestamp (MM/DD/YYYY, 12-hour time), location descriptor (e.g., “Front Desk,” “Locker Bay 2”), and notes on every transition with validation (no “Delivered” unless “Checked-in” exists). Built with Tauri + React for a responsive desktop UI and Rust for local business logic, all data persists in a local SQLite database with encrypted at-rest fields for sensitive items (e.g., partial masking for SSN-like identifiers if stored, and AES-encrypted notes/attachments index). Document and attachment management uses local file system storage with chunked/resumable transfers for large videos (default 25 MB chunks, resume after app restart), version control, tagging/search, and offline preview for common formats (PDF, PNG/JPG, TXT). Access control is enforced by tenant, role, and data scope; downloads apply a visible watermark (username + timestamp) and any “external link” is implemented as a locally generated, password-protected share package that expires after 7 days. Deposit and move-out settlement management tracks deposit hold/release, inspections, deduction line-items (amount, category, photo/video evidence), statement generation, and a two-step approval for refunds; “payout” produces a printable check request and ledger entry (no online payments). A configurable scheduling rules engine supports hard/soft constraints for staffing and inspection slots (unavailable times, capacity, required duration, consecutive vs. distributed sessions), with rule versioning and enable/disable controls. A local analytics and event-tracking framework records impressions/clicks/completions/conversions to drive funnel, retention, and quality metrics; dashboards render offline and exports produce CSV/JSON, while A/B experiments are configured locally by percentage split and start/end dates. The app must start in under 5 seconds on a typical office PC, include checkpoint-based state recovery after crashes, release file handles to prevent long-running leaks, and support offline update imports (signed update package from USB) with one-version rollback.
